sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].
Operating income grew faster, at a 20.5% CAGR to $155.2 billion, lifting operating margin from 30.1% to 46.8% [F31][F40][F223][F41][F50].
FY2026 was the sharpest step, with revenue up 17.8% to $331.8 billion driven by Microsoft Cloud, Azure within Intelligent Cloud and Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud [D472][F10][P17].
FY2018 broke the net-income line, falling 35.0% to $16.6 billion on the TCJA charge, and FY2019 rebounded 136.8% as that charge did not repeat [D48][F52][D101][P61].
Microsoft Cloud reached 64.6% of revenue in FY2026 and contributed 16.2pp of the 17.8% growth, up from 41.1% of revenue in FY2021 [D566][D568][D472][D553].
Server products and cloud services added 11.0pp in FY2026 as Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 41% on demand across workloads [D642][P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services contributed 5.1pp, with cloud revenue up 17% on Copilot and E5 revenue per user and seats up 6% [D649][P14].
Operating costs grew 10.3pp slower than revenue in FY2026, and incremental operating margin was 53.3% [D499][D498].
Diluted EPS rose 31.6% against net income growth of 31.3% as the diluted share count fell 0.2% [D476][D474][D493].
Operating margin of 46.8% in FY2026 sits above the 41.7% window median and at the window high, while gross margin of 67.9% is below its 68.2% median [F50][D975][D974][F30][D981].
Cost of revenue took 0.9pp off operating margin in FY2026 as AI infrastructure investment and Azure mix weighed on Intelligent Cloud gross margin [D500][P11].
R&D added 0.8pp and other lines 1.2pp, with operating expenses up 7% on R&D compute, AI talent and XBOX impairment [D501][D502][P16].
Net margin of 40.3% sat 6.5pp below the 46.8% operating margin, as other income of $10.7 billion from OpenAI gains partly offset a 19.4% tax rate [F70][F50][X124][D458][P7].
Operating cash flow of $182.9 billion was 1.37x net income, in line with the 1.34x of FY2025 [F100][D459][D405].
That rise was driven by higher cash received from customers and lower income tax payments, offset by more paid to suppliers [P1].
Free cash flow fell 6.5% to $67.0 billion, only 0.50x net income against a 0.91x window median, as capex rose 79.6% to $115.9 billion [D478][F120][D460][D990][D479][F110].
Capex reached 34.9% of revenue and 3.38x D&A, and free cash flow margin of 20.2% is the window low [D455][D461][D456][D982].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, 22.0% of revenue, against a -7.2% peer median and in the 83rd percentile of six software peers [D465][D466][D1007][D1006].
Total debt fell 6.6% to $40.3 billion while cash and investments rose 2.9% to $113.2 billion [D495][D464][D494][D463].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion plus dividends of $26.4 billion used 72.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted count fell 0.2% [X147][X157][D468][D493].
The current ratio of 1.23x is the window low, but the net cash cushion and $76.8 billion of cash and short-term investments leave liquidity ample [F200][D991][P2].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2025 and FY2026, at 0.70x and 0.50x [R1][D406][D460].
The gap is capex-led rather than earnings-led, so the risk is whether the AI build converts into revenue before depreciation and free cash flow stay compressed [D461][D456].
FY2017 pretax income, tax and receivables were later restated, and the pack keeps the first-reported values [R2][R3][R4][X95][X105][X213].
That affects only FY2017 comparisons, so no conclusion here rests on them.
Whether free cash flow margin recovers above the 30.3% window median from 20.2% in FY2026, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D984][D456].
Whether capex as a share of revenue falls back below the 22.9% of FY2025 from 34.9% in FY2026, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D401][D455].
Whether operating margin holds above the 41.7% window median from 46.8% in FY2026, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D975][F50].
